about.title: What this site is — and who is behind it.
sitePurpose: matuz.dev is my corner of the web: a portfolio, a working record, and a place to think out loud about software.

It exists for two reasons. First, so that anyone considering working with me can see what I build, how I work, and what I care about — without a recruiter in the middle. Second, as a project in its own right: everything here is designed, built, and maintained by me, from the design system to the deployment pipeline.
If you want the short version: I build software for whatever needs building, and this site is where that work speaks for itself.

whoAmI.title: Hi, I'm Rodrigo.
whoAmI.intro: I'm a full-stack software engineer based in Brazil, working remotely with individuals, teams, and companies of all sizes. I care about pragmatic engineering: the right solution for the problem at hand, whether that is building something from scratch, integrating with what exists, or carefully improving a legacy system.
bio: I hold a Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering from UniCesumar, and I've been building software professionally since 2024 through my own practice, MTZ Soft — covering the full lifecycle: requirements, development, testing, release, infrastructure, and production maintenance.

Before that, I led quality engineering squads at Compass UOL, coordinating testers across five web products and combining functional, exploratory, and risk-based testing with automation in Robot Framework and Postman. That experience shaped how I write software today: testability, clear documentation, and respectful failure modes are features, not afterthoughts.

On the open-source side, I contributed roughly 30% of the features of a Discord bot and web server used by 30+ servers and around 4,000 users, and I maintain a cross-platform desktop wallpaper application built with Rust, Tauri, and FFmpeg.

beyondWork.title: What I tinker with.
paragraphs: Outside of client work I run NixOS on my personal machine — currently learning my way around it and slowly rebuilding my environment as declarative configuration. Reproducibility as a daily habit, not just a buzzword.
My desktop runs the Caelestia shell, and I'm planning to publish my Nix configuration and dotfiles soon — once they're presentable enough to be read by strangers.
This side of things has no deadline and no deliverable: it's where I break things on purpose, then write down how I fixed them.

whoAmI.closing: The rest is on the home page — what I do, how I work, and how to reach me.
